---
title: "Use from R"
---

ggp-client is a Python package. From R you can use it with [reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/):
the downloading and consolidating run as ggp-client commands, and you read the result in R, with its labels.

## Install

```r
install.packages("reticulate")
library(reticulate)

virtualenv_create("ggp")                               # needs Python 3.10 or later
virtualenv_install("ggp", c("git+https://github.com/jossl95/ggp_client", "pyarrow"))
use_virtualenv("ggp", required = TRUE)
```

`pyarrow` is only needed to turn a polars table into an R data frame (below).

## Log in

Put the access link in your user-level `~/.Renviron` (`usethis::edit_r_environ()`), never in a script or project:

```
GGP_ACCESS_URL=<the link the portal emailed you>
```

Restart R. The first download saves the session in `data/.session.json`, so the link is used once. Treat it like a
password (see [Getting started](getting-started.qmd)).

## Download and consolidate GGS-II

Run the steps as commands of the Python in your environment. They start worker processes, which is safer in a normal
Python process than inside R's embedded one.

```r
ggp <- function(...) {
  if (system2(py_exe(), c("-m", "ggp_client.cli", ...)) != 0) stop("ggp-client failed")
}

ggp("sync")
ggp("download",    "--project", "ggs", "--round", "2", "--ext", "dta")
ggp("preprocess",  "--project", "ggs", "--round", "2")
ggp("consolidate", "--project", "ggs", "--round", "2")
```

This writes `data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet` and `.meta.json`, as in [GGS-II](ggs-ii.qmd). Everything
is relative to R's working directory; `ggp("--data-dir", "elsewhere", "sync")` uses another folder.

## Read the data and the labels

```r
library(reticulate)
read <- import("ggp_client.read")

path <- "data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet"

# a lazy polars table: pick the columns first, so only those are read and converted
df <- read$scan(path)$select(c("ggp_country", "dem01", "age"))$collect()$to_pandas()

meta <- jsonlite::read_json("data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.meta.json")
meta$column_labels$dem01            # "Gender"
vl <- meta$value_labels$dem01       # list: code -> label
vl[["1"]]                           # "Male"
```

reticulate turns the pandas table into an R data frame. The whole of GGS-II wave 1 (185,660 rows, 4,001 columns) is
large, so select the columns you need.

Apply the labels as a factor. A label may belong to several codes, which `factor()` allows:

```r
df$gender <- factor(df$dem01, levels = as.integer(names(vl)), labels = unlist(vl))
table(df$ggp_country, df$gender)
```

The meta file is plain JSON, with codes as text (`"1"`). Without Python, `arrow::read_parquet(path)` reads the
parquet file too.

## One file, straight from the portal's formats

`ggp_client.read` also reads a single `.dta` or `.sav` and returns its labels as they are in the file:

```r
m <- read$meta("data/download/raw/ggs-ii/w1/at/ggs2_w1_at_v1.1/.../ggsii_wave1_at_v_1_1.dta")
names(m)                            # file_label, column_labels, value_labels, missing_ranges, original_types
```
